:::{#exm-deriv-quadratic-form}

#### Derivative of a quadratic form

Let $\matr{S} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$ ($2 \times 2$, symmetric and constant)
and $\vcoef = \tp{(\coef{1}, \coef{2})}$.
Then $\tp{\vcoef}\matr{S}\vcoef = 3\coef{1}^2 + 2\coef{1}\coef{2} + 2\coef{2}^2$.
By @cor-quadratic-form-symmetric:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}(\tp{\vcoef}\matr{S}\vcoef)}_{2 \times 1}
&= 2 \matr{S} \vcoef \\
&= 2 \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \coef{1} \\ \coef{2} \end{pmatrix} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix} 6\coef{1} + 2\coef{2} \\ 2\coef{1} + 4\coef{2} \end{pmatrix}
\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating component-wise directly:

$$
\begin{pmatrix} \deriv{\coef{1}}(3\coef{1}^2 + 2\coef{1}\coef{2} + 2\coef{2}^2) \\ \deriv{\coef{2}}(3\coef{1}^2 + 2\coef{1}\coef{2} + 2\coef{2}^2) \end{pmatrix}
= \begin{pmatrix} 6\coef{1} + 2\coef{2} \\ 2\coef{1} + 4\coef{2} \end{pmatrix}
$$

Both methods agree.

For a matrix that is not symmetric, such as $\matr{S} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$,
@thm-quadratic-form gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\matr{S} + \tp{\matr{S}}) \vcoef
&= \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 6 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \coef{1} \\ \coef{2} \end{pmatrix} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix} 2\coef{1} + 2\coef{2} \\ 2\coef{1} + 6\coef{2} \end{pmatrix},
\end{aligned}
$$

which matches differentiating $\tp{\vcoef}\matr{S}\vcoef = \coef{1}^2 + 2\coef{1}\coef{2} + 3\coef{2}^2$ directly.

:::
